transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-04
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Head of ML, Emberwood), Samir Patel (Platform Eng), Olivia Ruiz (CTO)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics and cost attribution for Emberwood's planned chat/assistant rollout. Discussion covered per-route dashboards, token-level cost, retention/sampling, and enterprise security. A few typo/artifact in auto-transcript.

[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll keep this tight — around 40 minutes — Maya from Redwood, and Diego our SE will do the deep bits. lena, samir, olivia, thanks for being here.
[00:00:18] Lena (Emberwood): thanks maya, excited to see the console. we're trying to understand cost before commit, and want to see real per-route numbers, not just aggregate.
[00:00:30] Diego (Redwood SE): great, i'll share my screen — starting on the usage analytics page — apologies if the screen share lags a little.
[00:00:45] Speaker 1: (mumble) screen coming through now.
[00:01:10] Diego: ok the default view is a time-series of total tokens and requests. top-left you can select model family, route, and environment (hosted/dedicated). i'll click into a single route — "customer-support-chat" — and you see per-minute RPS, p50/p95 latency, and token breakdown by input/output.
[00:01:45] Lena: are those token counts post-tokenizer or pre? we need to reconcile with our billing meter.
[00:01:53] Diego: good q — it's post-tokenizer, and we show both raw tokens and billing tokens (some models have different tokenization). note there's a small delta sometimes because of special chars.
[00:02:20] Samir: can you break cost down by model variant? we run a mix of small and large models across routes.
[00:02:28] Diego: yeah, go to the cost breakdown tab — this is per-route/per-model. you can see cost per 1k tokens, cost per request bucket, and the cumulative monthly spend estimate. i'll filter to last 30 days and group by model.
[00:02:54] Diego: (click) here you can see a stacked bar — gptx-8k-like (labelled in console as G8) shows higher token cost but lower lat distribution because we batch it differently. smaller quantized models show cheaper per-token cost but higher tail latency on cold starts.
[00:03:22] Olivia: question — how accurate are these cost numbers vs actual invoice? we have to reconcile with finance.
[00:03:30] Maya: they're estimates based on current rate card + actual per-token execution metrics. they reconcile to invoice within 3-7%, but for committed dedicated customers we provide a more exact forecast.
[00:03:45] Lena: What about caching? can we see savings from prefix or KV cache?
[00:03:52] Diego: yes — cache hit rates are a first-class metric. on the console there's a cache analytics panel — shows hit ratio, token-savings, and dollar-saved estimate. you can slice by route/time window.
[00:04:14] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) so if we enable prefix cache on support route we'd save up to 40% token cost on repeated flows, depends on prompt patterns.
[00:04:35] Samir: latency SLOs — we need p99 < 200ms for some routes, can you show how p99 maps to model choice and deployment mode?
[00:04:44] Diego: yep — we have a per-route latency SLO panel. (navigates) here you can see p50/p95/p99 by model and by deployment (hosted vs dedicated). dedicated reservers give steady tail lat but cost more. you can set alert thresholds that notify slack or webhook.
[00:05:15] Lena: do alerts include regression detection for quality (like hallucination spike) or it's only latency/error?
[00:05:22] Maya: we do quality regressions tied to evals — you can upload prompt sets and Redwood will run periodic evals and surface quality regressions; console ties that into alerts too.
[00:05:35] Olivia: ok interesting — we have regulatory constraints, SOC2 is a must. do you provide audit logs and KMS integration?
[00:05:44] Maya: yes SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS for encryption at rest, and full audit logs available for export. i'll send the security pack after this call.
[00:05:58] Samir: are the audit logs queryable in console or do we need to pull them to SIEM?
[00:06:04] Diego: both — quick view in console and an export to S3 or to your SIEM via webhook.

[00:06:30] (20 minute demo walkthrough continues with clicks and filters)

[00:06:30] Diego: now i'm opening per-route details — see a timeline of token distribution by role (system/user/assistant), average cost per request, and a histogram of request sizes. this helps to identify routes that have high output tokens (expensive).
[00:07:05] Lena: can we group similar routes? our naming is messy across teams.
[00:07:10] Diego: yep you can tag routes and build route groups; grouping yields aggregated dashboards and rollup costs. we also have a route map export for finance.
[00:07:30] Maya: quick qualifying q — what's your expected traffic shape for pilot? daily tokens and % of interactive low-latency routes vs batch?
[00:07:40] Lena: pilot estimate: 5M tokens/day, 60% chat low-latency, 40% batch embeddings for search; target pilot duration 6 weeks.
[00:07:53] Maya: great that helps — i'll give you a rough cost estimation in follow up.

[00:08:20] Diego: switching to the retention and sampling settings — by default we sample 1% of requests for full content storage and higher sample for errors. you can change retention windows and sampling rates per route to balance visibility vs data retention costs.
[00:08:40] Samir: need to ensure PII redaction — do you support automatic redaction or do we do it client-side?
[00:08:47] Diego: we recommend client-side redaction for strict PII, but console also supports configurable redaction rules and regex-based filters; logs can be redacted before export.

[00:09:20] Lena: what about model rollouts? if we push a new model and perf regressions show up, can we auto-roll back?
[00:09:28] Diego: yes — the rollout manager supports canary, A/B, automated rollback on latency or quality regressions. the dashboard shows the rollout weight and metrics per variant.

[00:09:55] Olivia: compliance question — private deployment options? VPC or on-prem?
[00:10:02] Maya: Redwood Private offers customer-managed VPC options and on-prem packages for air-gapped envs; private control plane for larger enterprise. that's typically a different licensing track.

[00:10:30] (diego demonstrates per-route cost breakouts with an example)

[00:10:30] Diego: here's a sample monthly cost view for the support route: breakdown by model, caching, and batching savings. we annotated which parts are from caching vs batching. exportable CSV.
[00:10:55] Samir: can we get a CSV that shows cost per request id for a sample day?
[00:11:02] Diego: yes — request-level export with hashed ids for privacy. we can provide a spreadsheet.
[00:11:20] Speaker 3: (auto-transcript glitch) "cost per re quest"

[00:11:35] Maya: quick aside — a lot of customers ask about tokenization differences across models — we include a tokenizer tool in the console so you can paste a prompt and see token counts across models.
[00:11:50] Lena: good — that's been a painful reconciliation for us.

[00:12:20] Diego: moving to alerts — you can set alerting on cost burn rate so finance gets notified if daily spend > threshold; alert includes a snapshot link to the dashboard.
[00:12:38] Samir: do alerts support paging / on-call?
[00:12:42] Diego: yes integrations with PagerDuty, Slack, webhooks.

[00:13:05] Olivia: how does Redwood attribute cost for shared model pools? sometimes requests get routed to different hardware.
[00:13:13] Diego: cost attribution is route-centric by default but we also track hardware attribution; if you run dedicated pools we attribute to the pool id. routing analytics show percentage served by each pool.

[00:13:40] Lena: any examples of customers that reduced cost after enabling caching and smaller quantized models?
[00:13:47] Maya: yep — one retail customer reduced per-token spend ~35% using prefix caching + mixed model routing. we can share an anonymized case study.

[00:14:15] (short pause, background noise)
[00:14:40] Samir: technical deep dive request — we'd like to run a latency benchmark with our sample traffic; can you run on dedicated nodes?
[00:14:47] Diego: yes — for POC we can run benchmark runs on dedicated nodes. i'll need your sample traffic and route definitions. we'll provide a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:15:10] Lena: timeline — we're aiming to pick a vendor by mid-May so the pilot would need to start late April/early May.
[00:15:20] Maya: sounds doable — we can align POC scoping next week.

[00:15:45] Olivia: contract and legal — what does the procurement timeline look like?
[00:15:50] Maya: procurement typically takes 4-6 weeks for Dedicated/Private. hosted can be faster. we'll connect you to enterprise sales if you want to accelerate.

[00:16:10] (Diego toggles to the console's 'anomalies' tab)

[00:16:10] Diego: anomaly detection — console surfaces unexpected spikes in cost, latency, or hallucination rates. you can configure the sensitivity and run historical backfill.

[00:16:35] Samir: does anomaly detection use windowed baselines or ML models?
[00:16:40] Diego: hybrid — rolling baseline for simple anomalies, plus optional ML models trained on your traffic for more advanced detection.

[00:17:05] Lena: suggestion — we'd like to map alerts back to a root-cause link to the exact request example. is that possible?
[00:17:12] Diego: yes, console links alerts to sampled requests and the related traces. note we sample full request content by default at 1% to protect privacy.

[00:17:50] Maya: ok wrap-up — i'll send pricing and security docs; diego will share the benchmark sheet; lena/samir will send sample traffic. is anyone blocked on anything else?
[00:18:05] Lena: no blockers — main thing is clarity on cost for 5M tokens/day and p99 latency targets.
[00:18:12] Olivia: add a note: we may require KMS in a certain cloud region for data residency.
[00:18:18] Maya: noted, we'll include region support in the pack.

[00:18:45] (closing minutes: recap and explicit next steps)
[00:18:45] Maya: Recap: 1) Pricing + dedicated options (Maya) 2) Benchmark spreadsheet with tail-latency by route (Diego) 3) POC scoping call to define acceptance criteria and infra (Diego + Samir) 4) Security pack (SOC2/KMS/audit logs) (Maya).
[00:19:10] Samir: ok i'll loop in infra and legal after i have the security pack.
[00:19:20] Lena: thanks everyone — this was helpful.
[00:19:25] Maya: thanks — will follow up via email with links: security pack, pricing, benchmark sheet, sample dashboards.
